o.text: From Proto-Turkic *ālïn (“forehead”). Cognate with Turkish alın.

Morphologically, from çıx- (“to exit”) + -ış.
The sense 'appearance, speech' is a semantic loan from Russian выступле́ние (vystuplénije).
Cognates
Cognate with Turkish çıkış, Crimean Tatar çıqış, Karakhanid [script needed] (čïqïš, “going out, way out, profit”), Kazakh шығыс (šığıs, “exit”), Kyrgyz чыгыш (cıgış, “exit”), Uzbek chiqish (“exit, rising up”), etc.
Borrowed from Russian э́ллин (éllin), from Ancient Greek Ἕλλην (Héllēn).
From earlier lüqmə, from Arabic لُقْمَة (luqma).
